These CO2 estimates are "back-of-the-envelope" calculations to test if the new proposed gas-exchange proxy outlined in Franks et al. 2014 is reasonable (i.e., relative to previously published CO2 estimates). There are two main reasons why the estimates may not be reliable: 1) all stomatal size and density data come from the literature; new measurements were not made for the study; 2) leaf d13C was not measured; instead, a global compilation of published paleo-ci/ca data (age vs. ci/ca) was used to estimate ci/ca for the age of the fossil sample (via polynomial regression). Neither of these two things are recommended practices when applying the Franks model to fossils. NOTE: This estimate was previously reported using the stomatal index approach by van der Burgh et al., 1993.

These CO2 estimates are "back-of-the-envelope" calculations to test if the new proposed gas-exchange proxy outlined in Franks et al. 2014 is reasonable (i.e., relative to previously published CO2 estimates). There are two main reasons why the estimates may not be reliable: 1) all stomatal size and density data come from the literature; new measurements were not made for the study; 2) leaf d13C was not measured; instead, a global compilation of published paleo-ci/ca data (age vs. ci/ca) was used to estimate ci/ca for the age of the fossil sample (via polynomial regression). Neither of these two things are recommended practices when applying the Franks model to fossils. NOTE: This estimate was previously reported using the stomatal index approach by Kurschner et al., 1996.

These CO2 estimates are "back-of-the-envelope" calculations to test if the new proposed gas-exchange proxy outlined in Franks et al. 2014 is reasonable (i.e., relative to previously published CO2 estimates). There are two main reasons why the estimates may not be reliable: 1) all stomatal size and density data come from the literature; new measurements were not made for the study; 2) leaf d13C was not measured; instead, a global compilation of published paleo-ci/ca data (age vs. ci/ca) was used to estimate ci/ca for the age of the fossil sample (via polynomial regression). Neither of these two things are recommended practices when applying the Franks model to fossils. NOTE: This estimate was previously reported using the stomatal index approach by Kurschner et al., 1996.

These CO2 estimates are "back-of-the-envelope" calculations to test if the new proposed gas-exchange proxy outlined in Franks et al. 2014 is reasonable (i.e., relative to previously published CO2 estimates). There are two main reasons why the estimates may not be reliable: 1) all stomatal size and density data come from the literature; new measurements were not made for the study; 2) leaf d13C was not measured; instead, a global compilation of published paleo-ci/ca data (age vs. ci/ca) was used to estimate ci/ca for the age of the fossil sample (via polynomial regression). Neither of these two things are recommended practices when applying the Franks model to fossils. NOTE: This estimate was previously reported using the stomatal index approach by van der Burgh et al., 1993.

These CO2 estimates are "back-of-the-envelope" calculations to test if the new proposed gas-exchange proxy outlined in Franks et al. 2014 is reasonable (i.e., relative to previously published CO2 estimates). There are two main reasons why the estimates may not be reliable: 1) all stomatal size and density data come from the literature; new measurements were not made for the study; 2) leaf d13C was not measured; instead, a global compilation of published paleo-ci/ca data (age vs. ci/ca) was used to estimate ci/ca for the age of the fossil sample (via polynomial regression). Neither of these two things are recommended practices when applying the Franks model to fossils. NOTE: This estimate was previously reported using the stomatal index approach by van der Burgh et al., 1993.

Neither of these two things are recommended practices when applying the Franks model to fossils.

These CO2 estimates are "back-of-the-envelope" calculations to test if the new proposed gas-exchange proxy outlined in Franks et al. 2014 is reasonable (i.e., relative to previously published CO2 estimates). There are two main reasons why the estimates may not be reliable: 1) all stomatal size and density data come from the literature; new measurements were not made for the study; 2) leaf d13C was not measured; instead, a global compilation of published paleo-ci/ca data (age vs. ci/ca) was used to estimate ci/ca for the age of the fossil sample (via polynomial regression). Neither of these two things are recommended practices when applying the Franks model to fossils.

These CO2 estimates are "back-of-the-envelope" calculations to test if the new proposed gas-exchange proxy outlined in Franks et al. 2014 is reasonable (i.e., relative to previously published CO2 estimates). There are two main reasons why the estimates may not be reliable: 1) all stomatal size and density data come from the literature; new measurements were not made for the study; 2) leaf d13C was not measured; instead, a global compilation of published paleo-ci/ca data (age vs. ci/ca) was used to estimate ci/ca for the age of the fossil sample (via polynomial regression). Neither of these two things are recommended practices when applying the Franks model to fossils.
